line: The twenty-two trumps, which Crowley places on the Paths of the Tree of Life and reads in sequence from the Fool to the Universe.

sections.title: Twenty-two
sections.line: The count comes from the Hebrew alphabet, and the trumps are set between the Sephiroth.

quotes.quote: The letters of the Hebrew alphabet are twenty‐two.
so that their position on the Tree of Life is significant.

sections.title: The Paths
sections.line: Crowley relates the trumps to the twenty-two Paths. He calls the lines between the Sephiroth Forces of Nature.

quotes.quote: joined together their ten numbers on the Tree of Life by twenty‐two Paths.
The lines joining them are Forces of Nature, of a much less complete type;

sections.title: From the Fool to the Universe
sections.line: Crowley's own reading of the first and last trumps frames the series as one process.

quotes.quote: The Fool is the negative issuing into manifestation; the Universe is that manifestation, its purpose accomplished, ready to return.
The Universe, so states the theme, is the Celebration of the Great Work accomplished.

sections.title: What is not claimed here
sections.line: Crowley does not give the trumps an archetype reading. The field's tie to the Self is a site reading, and this page states no more than the sequence above.
